newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar steady in Tokyo, top heavy at 126.50 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar steady in Tokyo, top heavy at 126.50 yen.

text.p: 0007 GMT --*Dollar steadied against yen and mark in directionless early Tokyo amid lack of incentives.
*Stop-loss buying expected at around 126.50-55 yen, but exporters willing to sell dollars around there, dealers said.
*Downside solid due to investor buying interest below 126 yen and dollar strength against European currencies overnight.
*Light commercial dollar buying expected to emerge ahead of local fixing at 0100 GMT, said a Japanese bank dealer.
*Heavy selling interest from U.S. and European investors seen above 1.72 marks, making it heavy at around 1.7180 marks.
*"It's very difficult to find a new direction from the current level," said a European bank dealer.
*"There is still lingering worry over possible Bank of Japan dollar-selling intervention near 127 yen," he added.
*But some dealers said worries over dollar-selling intervention are fading, which may make it possible for dollar to rise even before Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) meeting.

*"(The monetary authorities) are worried about the speed of the dollar's rise against the yen. But I don't think there will be any urgent reasons to rectify that situation greatly," said another Japanese bank dealer.
*Japanese investors seen unwilling to buy dollars aggressively at current level, waiting instead to buy on dips.
*Japanese exporters likely to arrange forward dollar sales ahead of "Golden Week" holiday period here starting next week.
*News that Peruvian troops had stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima and rescued hostages would have no impact on the dollar/yen rate, dealers said.

*Dollar/mark rose overnight on news that group of six leading German economic research institutes predicted in a semi-annual report that the dollar would trade at an average rate of 1.80 marks in 1998.
*The European bank dealer said mark was likely to find support at around 73.50 yen and fresh buying around that point may also help push mark higher against U.S. dollar.
*Mark stood at around 73.65 yen at 0028 GMT, against 73.81 yen in late Tokyo trade on Tuesday.
